fatal_errors: The proposed boron substitution is not supported by either cited passage; E1 only discusses phosphorus-containing alloys generally, while E2 concerns other microalloying elements in Pd–Ni–P and reports little glass-forming benefit for several additions.
The intervention misses the central compositional change: increasing Fe and Co, reducing Mn, and lowering phosphorus to 15 at.% to promote eutectic-dominated solidification.
It predicts a broader supercooled-liquid region and a single DSC exotherm, whereas the reported modified alloy showed no detectable glass transition and crystallized in three stages.
The processing boundaries are not tied to the demonstrated conditions of approximately 20 μm ribbon melt-spun at 40 m/s and DSC reheating at 20 K/min.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the general challenge and proposes a clear, falsifiable comparison using DSC and structural characterization. It also correctly expects rapid quenching to favor amorphous retention and slow cooling to permit crystallization. However, it is not a reconstruction of the reported intervention or mechanism. The target altered the Fe/Co/Mn balance and reduced P to 15 at.%, producing more cooperative eutectic solidification; complete amorphization was then obtained specifically by melt spinning. The boron-based packing-frustration mechanism is generic and lacks relevant supporting evidence. Its predicted single crystallization peak and measurable supercooled-liquid interval also conflict with the observed three-stage devitrification and absence of a detected glass transition. Thus, although experimentally testable as a new idea, it is insufficiently evidenced to qualify as a supported plausible alternative.
